comparison: Perfect agreement on C8-C9 (novel isoforms). Both evaluations find the RNA-seq and RT-PCR validation convincing and mark as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.
Perfect agreement on C18-C19 (exclusion of GR inhibition mechanisms). Both evaluations find the negative findings well-supported and list as a strength with no concerns.
Perfect agreement on C32 (sexual dimorphism). Both evaluations find this integrative conclusion well-supported, with the editor explicitly calling it a 'valuable finding.'

Strong agreement on C4-C7 (GR expression characterization). Both evaluations find the immunofluorescence data convincing. OpenEval also includes C29 in this group; peer review marks all as SUPPORTED with no concerns.

Disagreement on C10-C13 (lack of GR function in fetal oocytes). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED across multiple platforms. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN due to low statistical power and questions why knockout shows no effect when GR is already nuclear.
Strong agreement on C23-C26 (male germline splicing regulation). Both evaluations find the RNA-seq and qPCR validation convincing and mark as SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C31 in this group.

Disagreement on C14-C16 (differential transcriptional response). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with statistical validation. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about indirect effects from systemic Dex and potential subtle consequences.
Agreement on C20-C21 (male GR expression pattern). Both evaluations find the immunofluorescence characterization well-supported. OpenEval also includes C28 in this group.

Agreement on C27 (fertility findings). Both evaluations find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes confounding effects of Prdm1-Cre but finds statistical analysis appropriate. Peer review acknowledges negative findings help rule out specific GR roles. OpenEval also includes C48.

Partial overlap on C17 (GR nuclear translocation despite lack of transcriptional activity). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as evidence of post-translational inactivation. Peer review groups C17 with C14-C16 and marks UNCERTAIN, questioning whether in vivo administration achieves same nuclear translocation as ex vivo.

Disagreement on C30 (lack of GR function in fetal oocytes, part of broader claim set). OpenEval groups C30 with C10-C13 and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C30 separately as UNCERTAIN, noting 'convincing evidence' but raising concerns about missed interaction effects and statistical power.

Agreement on C31 (GR-mediated splicing in male germline). OpenEval groups C31 with C23-C26 and finds SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C31 separately and also finds it SUPPORTED with 'convincing evidence.'
OpenEval finds C49 (knockout model validation) SUPPORTED with thorough validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific methodological claim.
OpenEval finds C1, C2, C33 (background literature on GR and stress) SUPPORTED as accurate summaries. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval finds C3, C34 (general GR mechanism knowledge) SUPPORTED as established scientific knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval marks C59-C63, C67 (speculative hypotheses about mechanisms) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative claims.
OpenEval finds C35-C58, C64-C66 (extensive background literature) SUPPORTED as accurate representations of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
